title: Mammalian Cell Encapsulation in Alginate Beads Using a Simple Stirred Vessel
protocol: Prepare the process buffer using 10 mM HEPES and 170 mM NaCl, then adjust the pH to 7.4.
Prepare the culture medium using Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 6 mM glutamine, 100 U/mL penicillin, and 100 mg/mL streptomycin.
Weigh the appropriate amount of alginate powder for the desired final concentration in beads.
Place 20 mL process buffer into an autoclavable glass jar on a magnetic stir plate.
Progressively add sodium alginate powder to the solution.
Stir the solution overnight at ~200 rpm.
If necessary, fasten the bottle onto a rotary mixer and continue mixing at 37 °C for an additional 24 h.
Sterilize the alginate solution by autoclaving for 30 min in a vessel that is less than half full.
Allow the temperature to decrease below 60 °C before retrieving the solution.
If necessary, remove particles by filtering the alginate solution shortly after autoclaving before it reaches room temperature.
Weigh out CaCO3 powder for preparation of calcium carbonate suspension.
Autoclave the CaCO3 suspension for 30 min.
Autoclave the stirred vessel used for the emulsification process.
Prepare the acidified oil immediately before the emulsification process by dissolving acetic acid in mineral oil.
Dissolve 44 µL acetic acid per 11 mL mineral oil placed in a 50 mL conical tube.
Ensure that the acetic acid is completely dissolved in the oil by repeated vortexing.
Allow all solutions to reach room temperature before proceeding to cell encapsulation.
Place 10 mL light mineral oil in the spinner flask.
Start agitation at a low rotation speed (e.g., 250 rpm).
Apply trypsin to suspend adherent cultured cells if used.
End the reaction by adding FBS-containing medium or trypsin inhibitor.
Collect a sample for cell enumeration.
Determine cell concentration and viability after Trypan blue staining using a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Centrifuge the cells for 7 min at 300 x g.
Wash the cells once in the desired medium containing emulsifiers like FBS or BSA (e.g., DMEM with 10% FBS).
Re-suspend the cell pellet in the same medium to obtain a 10.5-fold concentrated stock.
Add 1.1 mL of the 10.5-fold concentrated cell stock to 9.9 mL of alginate solution.
Add 550 µL of CaCO3 suspension and mix with a sterile spatula for even distribution.
Immediately transfer 10.5 mL of the alginate, cell, and CaCO3 mixture into the agitating oil using a syringe.
Aspirate and eject the mixture very slowly for highly viscous solutions.
Increase agitation rate immediately after adding alginate, cell, and CaCO3 mixture to oil.
Emulsify the alginate for 12 min.
Add 10 mL of oil and acetic acid solution to acidify emulsion.
Allow 8 min for acidification step.
Reduce agitation rate to 400 rpm.
Add 40 mL of process buffer mixed with 10% medium.
Stop the agitation after 1 minute.
Transfer the mixture to 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Rinse the spinner flask with an additional 20 mL medium and add this to the tube.
Aspirate as much aqueous phase as possible from the spinner flask before aspirating the oil phase.
Centrifuge the tubes for 3 minutes at 630 x g.
Remove the oil and excess aqueous solution by aspirating with a Pasteur pipette.
Wash the beads at least once with medium.
Filter the bead suspension on 40 µm nylon cell strainers.
Aspirate excess liquid associated with the beads from below the strainer.
Transfer the beads into a known volume of medium using a sterile spatula.
Measure the bead volume by volume displacement and top up the medium to obtain the desired bead:total volume ratio, typically 1 mL beads in 4 mL medium.
Transfer encapsulated cells into T-flasks for culture or transplantation experiments.
Stain beads with toluidine blue-O to quantify bead size distribution.
Place 0.5 ml beads into 4 ml process buffer containing 10% complete medium.
Add 500 μl of a 1 g/L toluidine blue solution prepared in process buffer.
Incubate for 60 min at 50 rpm on a rotary shaker.
Add 5 mL process buffer containing 10% complete medium.
Transfer beads and solution into a Petri dish.
Acquire images on a low-magnification microscope or using a hand-held digital camera.
Place the Petri dish on a light box if needed to enhance contrast and avoid shadows.
Perform image analysis to quantify bead size distribution as previously described.
Stain cells with ethidium homodimer to identify dead cells.
Stain cells with calcein AM to identify live cells.
Add 1 volume of beads to 4 volumes of process buffer containing 10% complete medium.
Add 4 µM calcein AM stock solution.
Add 2 µM ethidium homodimer stock solution.
Incubate the beads on ice for 20 min.
Place the solution between a slide and coverslip using a spacer to avoid compressing the beads.
Proceed to fluorescence microscopy.
Use single stain controls to assess fluorescence bleed-through.
Select appropriate fluorescence filters based on excitation/emission wavelengths associated with calcein AM (494/517 nm) and ethidium homodimer bound to DNA (528/617 nm).
Recover cells from the beads for further analysis by degelling alginate using citrate or another chelating solution.
Prepare a degelling solution containing 55 mM citrate, 10 mM HEPES and 95 mM NaCl at pH 7.4.
Mix the degelling solution with 10% medium.
Add 1 mL alginate beads to 9 mL of the mixture.
Degel the beads on ice with 75 rpm agitation for 20 min.
